items.question: When are Claude's peak hours?
items.answer: Claude's peak hours are weekdays from 13:00 to 19:00 UTC. All other hours, including the whole weekend, are off-peak.

items.question: What happens during peak hours?
items.answer: Your 5-hour session limit drains faster than usual on Free, Pro, Max and Team plans. Weekly limits don't change.

items.question: Is Claude in peak hours right now?
items.answer: Check the live clock at the top of this page. It shows the current status, the peak window in your local time and a countdown to the next change. Developers can query GET /api/status.

items.question: Which Claude plans are affected?
items.answer: Free, Pro, Max and Team. Enterprise plans aren't affected, and Claude Code on Pro and Max has been exempt since May 6, 2026.

items.question: What changed with Claude Code limits on September 14, 2026?
items.answer: Standard Claude Code weekly limits are now permanently 25% above the pre-promotion baseline. The temporary +50% boost ended the same day, so heavy users have about 17% less weekly capacity than during the promotion.

items.question: How can I get more out of my Claude limits?
items.answer: Run long or token-heavy work outside 13:00–19:00 UTC on weekdays, or on the weekend, when session limits drain at normal speed.

items.question: What was the March 2026 Claude promotion?
items.answer: From March 13 to 27, 2026, Claude doubled session limits outside weekday peak hours and all weekend for Free, Pro, Max and Team plans.

items.question: How does PromoClock verify AI deals?
items.answer: Every deal links to an official or reputable source, such as a help center article, the company's blog or a news report, and shows the date it was last checked. Expired offers leave the live lists automatically.

items.question: Is PromoClock affiliated with Anthropic?
items.answer: No. PromoClock is an independent project by Onur Şendere. Some outbound links are affiliate links, but they never decide which deals are listed.

disclosure.title: Affiliate disclosure
paragraphs: PromoClock is an independent project. Some links to AI tools on this site are affiliate or partner links. If you sign up or buy through one of them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.

Affiliate relationships never decide whether a deal is listed. We list offers that are publicly available from the tool's official channels, link to the original source, and show the date we last verified each one.
We only show promo codes that the tool publishes or that its partner program provides. Expired offers are removed from live lists automatically.
Tools without an affiliate program — including ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Midjourney — are covered in exactly the same way. PromoClock is not affiliated with Anthropic or any tool listed.
Questions? Email {email} or reach out on X at @onursendere.

sections.title: How we verify
sections.body: Every deal and limit change links to an official or reputable source: a help center article, an official blog post, an announcement from the company's own account or, for limit news, a reputable news report. We record the date we last checked each one and only publish codes the company or its partner program provides.

sections.title: How often it updates
sections.body: The site rebuilds every day. Deal status is calculated from start and end dates, so expired offers leave the live lists automatically, and the peak-hours clock runs live in your browser.

privacy.metaDescription: What PromoClock collects, why Google Analytics runs only with your consent, which cookies and local storage the site uses, and how to change your choice.
privacy.title: Privacy & cookies
privacy.intro: PromoClock collects as little as it can. This page explains what is processed when you visit, which cookies and storage the site uses, and how to change your mind at any time.

sections.title: Who is responsible
sections.body: PromoClock is run by Onur Şendere in Shrewsbury, UK, who is the data controller for this site. For privacy questions or requests, email {email} or message @onursendere on X.

sections.title: When you visit
sections.body: To deliver pages and keep the site secure, our hosting server and Cloudflare, which sits in front of it, process technical data from each request: your IP address, browser and device type, the page you asked for and the time. We don't use this data to identify or profile you. The /api/status endpoint keeps a one-way hash of your IP address for a few minutes to enforce its rate limit.

sections.title: Google Analytics, only with your consent
sections.body: If you choose “{accept}”, your browser loads Google Analytics 4 so we can count visits and see which pages are useful. It records the pages you view, the site that sent you, your approximate location (country and city, derived from your IP address), your device, browser, operating system, screen size and language, and interactions such as scrolling and clicks on outbound links. These are linked to a random ID stored in the _ga cookies. Google Analytics doesn't store IP addresses. Advertising features stay off: Google signals, ad personalisation and ad storage are disabled. If you choose “{reject}” or don't choose, Google Analytics isn't loaded and nothing is sent to Google.

sections.title: Legal basis
sections.body: Google Analytics runs only with your consent (UK GDPR Article 6(1)(a) and regulation 6 of PECR; in the EU, GDPR Article 6(1)(a) and Article 5(3) of the ePrivacy Directive). Request data and the necessary storage listed below rely on our legitimate interest in running a secure site and on providing the features you use, which doesn't require consent.

sections.title: How long data is kept
sections.body: Google Analytics keeps event-level data for 14 months; after that only aggregated reports remain. The _ga cookies expire after 13 months. Your cookie choice is remembered for 6 months, then we ask again, or sooner if we change how we use cookies.

sections.title: International transfers
sections.body: Google and Cloudflare may process data in the United States and other countries. Both are certified under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework and its UK Extension, which covers these transfers.

sections.title: Your choices and rights
sections.body: You can change or withdraw your consent at any time with “{settings}” at the bottom of every page. Withdrawing stops measurement straight away and deletes the Google Analytics cookies from your browser. You can also ask to access, correct or delete your data, or object to or restrict its use; because analytics data is tied only to a random ID, we may not be able to match it to you. If you're unhappy with how your data is handled, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk) or your local data protection authority.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
sections.body: When this policy changes, we update the date at the top of this page. If a change affects cookies, the banner asks for your choice again.

privacy.storageIntro: Necessary items are saved only when you use the feature they belong to. They stay on your device, except the language cookie, which is sent to our server so the home page opens in your language. Analytics cookies are set only after you allow them.
